'''Santa Jeremy Ono''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FCAHS|}} ({{langx|ja|小野 三太}}; born November 23, 1962)<ref name="bcb">{{cite web |url=https://www.bcbusiness.ca/Here-comes-Santa-Ono |title=Here comes Santa Ono |last=Bula |first=Frances |date=November 4, 2016 |website=BCBusiness |access-date=July 13, 2022 |archive-date=April 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413191123/https://www.bcbusiness.ca/Here-comes-Santa-Ono |url-status=live }}</ref> is a Canadian-American [[Immunology|immunologist]].

Ono served in a variety of roles, including as the [[President of the University of Michigan|15th president]] of the [[University of Michigan]] from October 2022 to May 2025, as the [[List of presidents of the University of British Columbia|15th president]] of the [[University of British Columbia]] from 2016 to 2022, and as the 28th president of the [[University of Cincinnati]] from 2012 to 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cafley |first=Julie |title=Can the Role of University President Really Be that Easy? |url=https://www.policymagazine.ca/pdf/21/PolicyMagazineSeptemberOctober-2016-Cafley.pdf |url-status=live |access-date=September 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029181820/http://policymagazine.ca/pdf/21/PolicyMagazineSeptemberOctober-2016-Cafley.pdf |archive-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> Ono was selected to serve as the [[List of presidents of the University of Florida|14th president]] of the [[University of Florida]] in May 2025, but was rejected in early June by the [[Florida Board of Governors]] for the position.<ref name="UF">{{Cite web |title= UF Board of Trustees selects Dr. Santa J. Ono as the 14th president of the University of Florida |date= May 27, 2025 |url= https://news.ufl.edu/2025/05/ono-selection/ |access-date= May 27, 2025 |archive-date= May 27, 2025 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20250527232921/https://news.ufl.edu/2025/05/ono-selection/ |url-status= live }}</ref>

In August 2025, Ono was appointed president of the global division at the Ellison Institute of Technology, Oxford Limited, a private limited company incorporated in November 2021 in England.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |last=Eberbach |first=Jennifer |date=2025-08-18 |title=Santa Ono lands new job at United Kingdom institute |url=https://www.mlive.com/news/ann-arbor/2025/08/santa-ono-lands-new-job-at-united-kingdom-institute.html |access-date=2025-08-19 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web |title=ELLISON INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, OXFORD LIMITED overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/13773507 |access-date=2025-08-19 |website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref> He would be responsible for assisting John Bell, the company's president, in expanding its local science programs and overseeing its global affairs.<ref name=":14" />

==Early life and education==
Born in 1962, Santa Ono is the son of Japanese mathematician [[Takashi Ono (mathematician)|Takashi Ono]], who immigrated to the United States from Japan in the late 1950s. Ono was born in [[Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]], Canada, where his father worked as an assistant professor of mathematics at the University of British Columbia from 1961 to 1964. Ono has United States citizenship and Canadian citizenship.<ref name="bcb" />

Ono was raised in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], and [[Towson, Maryland]], where his father worked as a faculty member at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] from 1964 to 1969 and at [[Johns Hopkins University]] from 1969 to 2011, respectively.<ref name="bcb" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ono |first=Santa Jeremy |date=2023-03-07 |title=Inauguration Address {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/speeches/inauguration-address/ |url-status= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308005238/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/speeches/inauguration-address/ |archive-date=March 8, 2023 |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=president.umich.edu}}</ref> His older brother is Momoro Ono and his younger brother is [[Ken Ono]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biography {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/about/biography/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=president.umich.edu |archive-date=July 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713221601/https://president.umich.edu/about/biography/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Ono received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree with a major in [[biological sciences]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1984 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in [[experimental medicine]] from [[McGill University]] in Canada in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ono |first=Santa |date=September 28, 2018 |title=Brand-building in a Bowtie: A Presidential Perspective |url=https://www.theworld100.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Plenary-3-Santa-Ono-1.pdf |access-date=July 13, 2022 |website=The World 100 Reputation Network |page=2 |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714004532/https://www.theworld100.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Plenary-3-Santa-Ono-1.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==

At University College London, Ono served as associate dean of students and as a member of the University College London Council.<ref name="Hand">{{cite web |url=http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=16747|title=Santa Jeremy Ono Named President of the University of Cincinnati|work=UC News|date=October 23, 2012|accessdate=August 10, 2016|first=Greg|last=Hand|archive-date=October 25, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025162641/http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=16747|url-status=dead}}</ref> In June 2006, Ono was named to the newly created post of vice provost for academic initiatives at [[Emory University]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emory University News Release - SantaOno |url=https://www.emory.edu/news/Releases/SantaOno1150212904.html |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=www.emory.edu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528023558/emory.edu/news/Releases/SantaOno1150212904.html|archive-date=2010-05-28|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== University of Cincinnati ===
In June 2010, Ono was named senior vice president for academic affairs and provost at the University of Cincinnati.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=12110|title=Ono Named Provost at University of Cincinnati|date=June 22, 2010|first=Hand|last=Greg|work=UC News|publisher=Uc.edu|access-date=June 30, 2010|archive-date=September 9, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100909104524/http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=12110|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=12403 |title=Williams Challenges UC to Excel, Achieve |work=UC News |publisher=Uc.edu |date=September 19, 2010 |accessdate=October 23, 2010 |archive-date=September 27, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100927085211/http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=12403 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2012, Ono was named the 28th president of the University of Cincinnati in Ohio, becoming the first Japanese-American president of that university.<ref name="Hand" /> U Square at the Loop, a US$78 million mixed-use development, was opened during his presidency.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.multihousingnews.com/post/u-square-the-loop-finally-open-2/|title=U Square @ the Loop Finally Open|first=Adrian|last=Maties|work=MultiHousing News|access-date=December 19, 2016|archive-date=December 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220164410/https://www.multihousingnews.com/post/u-square-the-loop-finally-open-2/|url-status=dead|date=3 September 2013}}</ref> In January 2015, ''[[Inside Higher Ed]]'' named Ono as "the nation's most notable college president for 2015".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/education/2015/01/02/ono-named-most-notable-president-of-2015/21191495/|title=UC's Ono named 2015's most notable president|first=Henry|last=Molski|date=January 2, 2015|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-date=April 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402144446/http://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/education/2015/01/02/ono-named-most-notable-president-of-2015/21191495/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 19, 2015, [[Killing of Samuel DuBose|Samuel DuBose]], a Black unarmed motorist who was not affiliated with the university, was fatally shot by a University of Cincinnati police officer after DuBose was stopped off-campus for driving a car without a front license plate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=hlr |date=2016-02-10 |title=The Shooting of Samuel DuBose |url=https://harvardlawreview.org/print/vol-129/the-shooting-of-samuel-dubose/ |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=Harvard Law Review |language=en-US}}</ref> It sparked widespread protests for many days with some being arrested.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Felton |first=Ryan |date=2016-10-25 |title=Officer who shot Samuel DuBose faces murder trial as city braces for protests |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/oct/25/samuel-dubose-ray-tensing-trial-begins-police-fatal-shooting |access-date=2025-11-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> In January 2016, on the condition of Ono's formal apology, the university reached a US$4.85 million civil settlement with the family of Samuel DuBose.<ref>{{Cite web |last=LaFleur |first=Pat |date=2016-01-18 |title=UC to pay DuBose family $5.3M in settlement |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/local-news/hamilton-county/cincinnati/family-of-sam-dubose-settles-with-uc-for-48m-plus-free-tuition-for-12-children |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=WCPO 9 Cincinnati |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-01-19 |title=University of Cincinnati, family of Sam DuBose reach settlement |url=https://www.wlwt.com/article/university-of-cincinnati-family-of-sam-dubose-reach-settlement-1/3561634 |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=WLWT |language=en}}</ref>

=== University of British Columbia ===
On June 15, 2016, Ono was named the [[List of presidents of the University of British Columbia|15th president and vice chancellor]] of the [[University of British Columbia]] in Canada, effective August 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.ubc.ca/2016/06/13/ubcs-15th-president/|title=Dr. Santa Ono to become UBC President and Vice Chancellor|type=Media Release|date=June 13, 2016|work=UBC News|access-date=July 9, 2016|archive-date=July 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160717100525/http://news.ubc.ca/2016/06/13/ubcs-15th-president/|url-status=live}}</ref> He was re-appointed for a second five-year term on August 11, 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.ubc.ca/2020/08/11/professor-santa-j-ono-reappointed-as-president-and-vice-chancellor-of-ubc/|title=Professor Santa J. Ono reappointed as president and vice-chancellor of UBC|type=Media Release|date=August 11, 2020|work=UBC News|access-date=June 8, 2022|archive-date=July 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724103053/https://news.ubc.ca/2020/08/11/professor-santa-j-ono-reappointed-as-president-and-vice-chancellor-of-ubc/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2017, Ono reinstated [[John Furlong (sports administrator)|John Furlong]] as keynote speaker for a university fundraiser despite allegations of Furlong's abuse of Indigenous children during his time as a teacher in a remote community.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=McCabe |first=Samantha |title=Emails reveal UBC caved to donor backlash over Furlong affair |url=https://www.ubyssey.ca/news/emails-reveal-more-details-to-furlong-affair/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Ubyssey |date=April 26, 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-09-26 |title=John Furlong biography omits secret past in Burns Lake |url=https://www.straight.com/news/john-furlong-biography-omits-secret-past-burns-lake |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Georgia Straight |language=en}}</ref> Furlong's participation sparked protests from UBC students and activists, including some of his alleged victims.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Sharlandjieva |first=Vassilena |title=Students organize silent protest against Furlong's reinstatement as banquet keynote |url=https://www.ubyssey.ca/news/students-organize-silent-protest-furlongs-reinstatement/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Ubyssey |date=February 28, 2017 |language=en}}</ref> This incident led to the resignation of the only Indigenous member of UBC's Sexual Assault Policy Committee.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-01-11 |title=Indigenous professor quits UBC panel over John Furlong speech |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/british-columbia/indigenous-professor-quits-ubc-panel-over-john-furlong-speech/article33593666/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |work=The Globe and Mail |language=en-CA}}</ref> Ono's decision to reinvite Furlong followed reported pressure from wealthy donors.<ref name=":1" />

In June 2018, Ono's social media presence was noted by ''[[The Ubyssey]]'', the official UBC student newspaper, as lacking a clear distinction between his personal views and university policies, leading to ambiguity and sometimes prompting clarification from the university's Public Affairs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Board |first=Ubyssey Editorial |date=2018-06-08 |title=Editorial: Santa Ono's social media presence is blurring with university policy. That's a problem. |url=https://ubyssey.ca/opinion/social-media-maven/ |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=The Ubyssey |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McKenzie |first=Lindsay |date=June 14, 2018 |title=A College President's Twitter Strategy |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2018/06/15/drawing-line-between-policy-and-personality-twitter |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2019, [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] announced plans to establish Canada's first "Cloud Innovation Centre" at UBC.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-07-10 |title=First university-based Cloud Innovation Centre in Canada to open in early 2020 {{!}} AWS Public Sector Blog |url=https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/publicsector/first-university-based-cloud-innovation-centre-in-canada-to-open-in-early-2020/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=aws.amazon.com |language=en-US}}</ref> The project proceeded without community consultation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pathak |first=Sonia |title=UBC and Amazon's Cloud Innovation Centre is met with concerns from students and faculty |url=https://www.ubyssey.ca/news/ubc-and-amazon-partner-up/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Ubyssey |date=August 10, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Contract details were withheld until a student group obtained them through a freedom of information request. The documents showed that the Ono administration followed Amazon's directive to keep the CA$3 million funding for the use of university technology confidential.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cosh |first=Alex |date=2020-08-18 |title=We Took a Look at the President of UBC's Text Messages. Amazon Told Him to Keep a $3 Million Deal Secret. |url=https://pressprogress.ca/we-took-a-look-at-the-president-of-ubcs-text-messages-amazon-told-him-to-keep-a-3-million-deal-secret/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=PressProgress |language=en}}</ref>

In October 2019, at least six students were given medical attention for suspected drugging incidents at a fraternity party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Daflos |first=Penny |date=2019-10-02 |title=UBC meets with student as RCMP investigates roofie allegations |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/ubc-meets-with-student-as-rcmp-investigates-roofie-allegations/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=[[CTV News]] |language=en}}</ref> Following this, a female professor faced online abuse after criticizing the fraternities involvement in [[Remembrance Day]] ceremonies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pathak |first=Sonia |title=Professor's critique of fraternity participation in Remembrance Day ceremony provokes controversy, harassment |url=https://www.ubyssey.ca/news/professors-critiques-frats-remembrance/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Ubyssey |date=November 15, 2019 |language=en |archive-date=November 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221101111557/https://www.ubyssey.ca/news/professors-critiques-frats-remembrance/ |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the university administration, under the Ono presidency, responded and emphasized freedom of expression rather than condemning the harassment against the professor, affirming its "commitment to freedom of expression and academic freedom".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pathak |first=Sonia |title=Professor's critique of fraternity participation in Remembrance Day ceremony provokes controversy, harassment |url=https://ubyssey.ca/news/professors-critiques-frats-remembrance/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Ubyssey |date=November 15, 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

During Ono's tenure, the university hosted multiple controversial speakers promoting white supremacist, Islamophobic, and neo-Nazi movements, often invited by student groups with extreme views.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vescera |first=Zak |title=A splintered movement: How the far-right found a foothold on campus |url=https://www.ubyssey.ca/features/a-splintered-movement-far-right-on-campus/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Ubyssey |date=April 20, 2019 |language=en |archive-date=July 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730182254/https://www.ubyssey.ca/features/a-splintered-movement-far-right-on-campus/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Ono inaccurately claimed equal community support for an anti-trans speaker event,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cosh |first=Alex |date=2020-02-05 |title=Internal Emails Contradict the University of British Columbia's Explanation for Why it Hosted an 'Alt-Right' Event on Campus |url=https://pressprogress.ca/internal-emails-contradict-the-university-of-british-columbias-explanation-for-why-it-hosted-an-alt-right-event-on-campus/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=PressProgress |language=en}}</ref> leading to the Vancouver Pride Society's decision in July 2019 to ban UBC's participation in the [[Vancouver Pride Parade]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vancouver |first=Tessa Vikander Star |date=2019-07-10 |title=Banning UBC from Pride Parade is a welcomed 'kick in the pants,' says transgender professor |url=https://www.thestar.com/vancouver/banning-ubc-from-pride-parade-is-a-welcomed-kick-in-the-pants-says-transgender-professor/article_918c7a8b-93c5-5d0c-84d3-30597ba7c5be.html |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=Toronto Star |language=en}}</ref>

=== University of Michigan ===
On July 13, 2022, Ono was named as the [[President of the University of Michigan|15th president]] of the [[University of Michigan]], with his term beginning on October 13, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Regents appoint Santa Ono as University of Michigan's next president {{!}} The University Record |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/regents-appoint-santa-ono-as-university-of-michigans-new-president/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714004452/https://record.umich.edu/articles/regents-appoint-santa-ono-as-university-of-michigans-new-president/ |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=record.umich.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-13 |title=Santa Ono named University of Michigan's 15th president |url=https://www.michiganpublic.org/education/2022-07-13/santa-ono-named-university-of-michigans-15th-president |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Michigan Public |language=en}}</ref> He became the first Japanese-American to lead the university. In October 2023, Ono received a 4% raise in base salary, increasing it from US$975,000 to US$1,014,000 annually.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |title=UM president gets raise after first year in office, pushing salary past $1M |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2023/10/19/um-president-gets-raise-after-first-year-increasing-his-pay-past-1m/71244881007/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Under the Ono presidency, the university conducted a renovation of the [[President's House, University of Michigan|President's House]], the official residence of the university president, from 2022 to 2023 at a cost of US$11.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |title=Updated and more accessible: UM wraps up $11.5M in renovations to president's house |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2023/10/02/university-of-michigan-presidents-house-santa-ono-upgrades-renovations/70991020007/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US |archive-date=October 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231008232633/https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2023/10/02/university-of-michigan-presidents-house-santa-ono-upgrades-renovations/70991020007/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

During Ono's March 2023 address, he stated that DEI would be a major focus of his presidency.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inauguration Address {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/speeches/inauguration-address/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=president.umich.edu |archive-date=March 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308005238/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/speeches/inauguration-address/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wood |first=Peter W. |title=Opinion {{!}} Will DEI Return to the University of Florida? |url=https://www.wsj.com/opinion/will-dei-return-to-the-university-of-florida-santa-ono-reform-backward-progress-5010116e |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=WSJ |language=en-US |archive-date=May 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520035208/https://www.wsj.com/opinion/will-dei-return-to-the-university-of-florida-santa-ono-reform-backward-progress-5010116e |url-status=live }}</ref> In response to a donor's request for clarification on how the university spent money on DEI programs in 2023, Ono wrote, "I'm very proud of what has been accomplished and I'm excited about what's going to happen with DEI 2.0".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jesse |first=David |date=2025-05-15 |title=At U. of Michigan, Frustrations Grew Over a President Who Couldn't Be Pinned Down |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/at-u-of-michigan-frustrations-grew-over-a-president-who-couldnt-be-pinned-down |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref> In January 2024, the university was reported to have 241 employees in the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) offices, with payroll costs totaling more than US$30 million annually.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kabbany |first=Jennifer |date=2024-01-09 |title=UMich now has more than 500 jobs dedicated to DEI, payroll costs exceed $30 million |url=https://www.thecollegefix.com/umich-now-has-more-than-500-jobs-dedicated-to-dei-payroll-costs-exceed-30-million/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=The College Fix |archive-date=May 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250530053215/https://www.thecollegefix.com/umich-now-has-more-than-500-jobs-dedicated-to-dei-payroll-costs-exceed-30-million/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On March 27, 2025, citing the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration's]] executive order, Ono reversed his previous DEI policies and shut down the university's DEI programs and offices.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Altavena |first=John Wisely and Lily |title=University of Michigan, a longtime champion of progressive values, to close its DEI office |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/education/2025/03/27/university-michigan-dei-office-closing/82690676007/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Evolving our approach to DEI and moving forward together {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/evolving-our-approach-to-dei-and-moving-forward-together/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=president.umich.edu |archive-date=May 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515152848/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/evolving-our-approach-to-dei-and-moving-forward-together/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tucker |first=Emma |date=2025-03-28 |title=University of Michigan will end its DEI program, citing Trump executive order that 'began to reshape higher education' |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/03/27/us/university-of-michigan-eliminates-dei-program/index.html |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2023, Ono spent US$575,000 to purchase a house in the far Detroit suburb of [[West Bloomfield Township, Michigan|West Bloomfield Township]] in [[Oakland County, Michigan|Oakland County]], about 45 miles from Ann Arbor, despite his contract requiring residency in the President's House. ''[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]'' reported that Ono was often absent from campus and "missed numerous executive-officer-council meetings", which led to "a leadership void and squabbles in some cases".<ref name=":11" /> Ono stated in his primary residence tax exemption affidavit to the state of Michigan that he spends "100%" of his time at the Oakland County address, which he also used for voter registration and his driver's license.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |date=2024-07-30 |title=UM's Ono buys house in Oakland County, raising contract and tax questions |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2024/07/30/university-michigan-santa-ono-buys-house-oakland-county-raising-contract-tax-questions/74474294007/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=The Detroit News}}</ref> After he told the local newspaper ''[[The Detroit News]]'' in June 2024 that he lived in Oakland County only on occasional weekends or holidays, questions about his residency prompted a review by the local tax assessor, who in August found nothing against Ono's sworn affidavit of having his "only primary residence" in Oakland County instead of Ann Arbor.<ref name=":11" /><ref name=":12" /><ref name=":13">{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |date=Aug 11, 2024 |title=Assessor lets stand primary residence exemption for UM president on off-campus home |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/oakland-county/2024/08/11/west-bloomfiel-assessor-will-not-take-action-on-primary-residence-exemption-declared-by-um-president/74735820007/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref> The result aligned with concerns raised in the media about his failure to fulfill his contractual obligation to reside in the President's House in Ann Arbor, as his predecessors had done.<ref name=":13" /><ref name=":12" />

On October 17, 2024, the university's [[Regents of the University of Michigan|Board of Regents]] voted unanimously to extend Ono's contract by an additional eight years, through October 1, 2032.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jarvis |first1=Kay |date=October 10, 2024 |title=Regents extend President Ono's contract until 2032 |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/regents-extend-president-onos-contract-until-2032/ |accessdate=October 24, 2024 |website=record.umich.edu |publisher=The University Record |quote=(UPDATE: The Board of Regents unanimously voted to ratify the contract extension Oct. 17.)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Shanbom |first1=Matthew |last2=Chatlosh |first2=Ava |date=2024-10-18 |title=Regents approve neutrality bylaw, extends Ono contract to 2032 |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/umich-board-of-regents-approves-institutional-neutrality-bylaw-extends-ono-contract-to-2032/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |newspaper=[[The Michigan Daily]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The extension also increased Ono's base salary to US$1.3 million per year, a 33% rise since he started his tenure two years before.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |title=UM regents boost Ono's salary to $1.3M, a 33% increase in two years |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2024/10/17/university-of-michigan-regents-boost-santa-onos-salary-to-1-3m-a-33-increase-in-two-years/75717368007/#:~:text=In%20the%20extension,%20the%20regents,another%20eight%20years%20to%202032. |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref> Media reported that he used Florida's 2024 offer to get this pay increase.<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |last=Jesse |first=David |date=2025-05-15 |title=At U. of Michigan, Frustrations Grew Over a President Who Couldn't Be Pinned Down |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/at-u-of-michigan-frustrations-grew-over-a-president-who-couldnt-be-pinned-down |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref>

On January 10, 2025, Ono shut down the University of Michigan's two-decade-long partnership with [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] in China since 2005, terminating the UM–SJTU Joint Institute as well as the dual-degree and study-abroad programs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-11 |title=University of Michigan ends Chinese partnership after intense pressure from US lawmakers |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/university-michigan-ends-chinese-partnership-093000917.html |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=U-M to end partnership with Shanghai Jiao Tong University {{!}} The University Record |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/u-m-to-end-partnership-with-shanghai-jiao-tong-university/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=record.umich.edu |archive-date=January 11, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250111004302/https://record.umich.edu/articles/u-m-to-end-partnership-with-shanghai-jiao-tong-university/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 4, 2025, the day after giving a speech as the president on the University of Michigan's spring commencement,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spencer |first=Sarah |date=2025-05-05 |title=UMich hosts Spring 2025 Commencement ceremony |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/umich-hosts-spring-2025-commencement-ceremony/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US |archive-date=May 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250519080650/https://www.michigandaily.com/news/umich-hosts-spring-2025-commencement-ceremony/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Ono announced through a campus email that he became the sole finalist for the presidency of the [[University of Florida]] and decided to leave Michigan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leadership update – Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/leadership-update/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=president.umich.edu |archive-date=May 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250519100905/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/leadership-update/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-05-05 |title=University President Santa Ono announces departure from UMich |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/news-briefs/university-president-santa-ono-announces-departure-from-umich/ |access-date=2025-05-05 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US |archive-date=May 5, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250505010844/https://www.michigandaily.com/news/news-briefs/university-president-santa-ono-announces-departure-from-umich/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Ono submitted his resignation letter to the chair of the Board of Regents on the same day, resigning from all university employment, including his faculty position.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Eberbach |first=Jennifer |date=2025-06-20 |title=Santa Ono resigns from all employment at the University of Michigan |url=https://www.mlive.com/news/ann-arbor/2025/06/santa-ono-resigns-from-teaching-at-the-university-of-michigan.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref> On May 5, [[Rebekah Modrak]], chair of the university's Faculty Senate, said that many professors had complained that Ono's campus emails seemed to have been written by ChatGPT.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wisely |first=John |title=U-M's Santa Ono, leaving for University of Florida, gets mixed marks from students, staff |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2025/05/05/santa-ono-leaving-for-university-of-florida-reactions/83460844007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250518143422/https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2025/05/05/santa-ono-leaving-for-university-of-florida-reactions/83460844007/ |archive-date=May 18, 2025 |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US}}</ref> Katherine White, the chair of the Board of Regents, accepted Ono's resignation in writing on May 6.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Dodge |first=Samuel |date=2025-06-10 |title=Santa Ono's resignation letter hints at tension with University of Michigan regents |url=https://www.mlive.com/news/ann-arbor/2025/06/santa-onos-resignation-letter-hints-at-tension-with-university-of-michigan-regents.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref> Ono's tenure as president at the University of Michigan was the shortest of all past presidents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-09 |title=Editorial: UM should learn from Santa Ono saga |url=https://www.crainsdetroit.com/editorial/editorial-um-should-learn-santa-ono-saga |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Crain's Detroit Business |language=en}}</ref> The University of Michigan Board of Regents appointed [[Domenico Grasso]], the then-chancellor of the [[University of Michigan–Dearborn]], as the university's interim president on May 8.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Domenico Grasso becomes Interim President of University of Michigan {{!}} The University Record |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/domenico-grasso-becomes-interim-president-of-university-of-michigan/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=record.umich.edu |archive-date=May 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515162952/https://record.umich.edu/articles/domenico-grasso-becomes-interim-president-of-university-of-michigan/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Wisely |first=John |title=Domenico Grasso installed as University of Michigan's interim president |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/education/2025/05/15/domenico-grasso-university-of-michigan-interim-president/83601290007/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US |archive-date=May 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250518042928/https://www.freep.com/story/news/education/2025/05/15/domenico-grasso-university-of-michigan-interim-president/83601290007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Media reports noted that Ono did not comply with the clause in his contract that required him to give six-month advance notice of his voluntary resignation.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moody |first=Josh |title=Ono Resignation Letter Reflected Tensions With UM Board |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/quick-takes/2025/06/11/ono-resignation-letter-reflected-tensions-um-board |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref>

On June 27, 2025, Ono was sued as a defendant in a federal civil class action in the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan]] in Detroit by a group of female college athletes. They alleged that the Ono administration allowed an athletics coordinator to continue coaching and conceal his identity from students after learning that he had hacked into their accounts and stolen personal photos.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=McMann |first=Aaron |date=2025-06-28 |title=Jim Harbaugh, Santa Ono sued in expanding Matt Weiss hacking case |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/06/jim-harbaugh-santa-ono-sued-as-matt-weiss-hacking-case-expands.html |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Romo |first=Christian |title=Jim Harbaugh, former Michigan president Santa Ono sued in Matt Weiss hacking case |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/06/27/matt-weiss-jim-harbaugh-santa-ono-hacking-scandal/84393148007/ |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US}}</ref> The coordinator was indicted on 24 charges in federal court in March 2025,<ref name=":10" /> and the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] said that the hacking affected "more than 3,000 student-athletes", most of whom were women.<ref name=":9" />

==== Response to labor union protest ====
On March 7, 2023, the [[Graduate Employees' Organization 3550]], a labor union representing graduate student instructors at the university, disrupted the ceremonial procession during Ono's inauguration.<ref>{{cite news |date=2023-08-25 |title=GEO protest interrupts Ono's inaugural procession route |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/administration/geo-protest-interrupts-onos-inaugural-procession-route/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402194249/https://www.michigandaily.com/news/administration/geo-protest-interrupts-onos-inaugural-procession-route/ |archive-date=April 2, 2024 |accessdate=2024-04-02 |newspaper=The Michigan Daily}}</ref> On March 29, after negotiations broke down, the majority of GEO 3550 members went on [[Strike action|strike]], demanding a salary increase from US$24,000 to US$38,000.<ref name=":17" /> On April 5 and April 10, respectively, Chief Judge Carol Kuhnke of the Washtenaw County Trial Court denied the Ono administration's request for a [[temporary restraining order]] and a [[preliminary injunction]] to suspend the strike.<ref name=":17">{{cite news |date=2023-04-10 |title=Injunction denied in UM grad student strike |url=https://www.michiganpublic.org/education/2023-04-10/injunction-denied-in-um-grad-student-strike |accessdate=2024-04-02 |newspaper=Michigan Public NPR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Judge denies U of M request for order ending grad assistants’ strike  |url=https://michiganadvance.com/briefs/judge-denies-u-of-m-request-for-order-ending-grad-assistants-strike/ |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=Michigan Advance |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Court denies injunction to halt strike by graduate workers {{!}} The University Record |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/court-denies-injunction-to-halt-graduate-workers-strike/ |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=record.umich.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorable Carol Kuhnke {{!}} Washtenaw County, MI - Official Website |url=https://www.washtenaw.org/1443/Honorable-Carol-Kuhnke |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230401101842/www.washtenaw.org/1443/Honorable-Carol-Kuhnke |archive-date=2023-04-01 |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=www.washtenaw.org}}</ref>

On April 20, 2023, GEO members confronted Ono at a restaurant in Ann Arbor and blocked his car from leaving. Two protesters were arrested.<ref>{{cite news |date=2023-04-20 |title=2 GEO protesters detained and released in police encounter outside Ann Arbor restaurant |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/news-briefs/geo-protestors-detained/ |accessdate=2024-04-02 |newspaper=The Michigan Daily}}</ref> GEO later accused the Ono administration of invented false grades for students in classes taught by striking GEO members. The institutional accreditor [[Higher Learning Commission]] investigated and later dismissed those accusations.<ref>{{cite news |date=2023-06-16 |title=Fake grades scandal at University of Michigan leads to accreditation board investigation |url=https://michiganadvance.com/briefs/fake-grades-scandal-at-university-of-michigan-leads-to-accreditation-board-investigation/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402194250/https://michiganadvance.com/briefs/fake-grades-scandal-at-university-of-michigan-leads-to-accreditation-board-investigation/ |archive-date=April 2, 2024 |accessdate=2024-04-02 |newspaper=Michigan Advance}}</ref> As the strike extended into the spring, Ono reduced his attendance at campus events and his social media activity.<ref>{{cite news |date=2023-10-17 |title=A Very Public Presidency's Reality Check: Santa Ono's Casual Accessibility won him the job at the University of Michigan. His first year challenged that approach. |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/a-very-public-presidencys-reality-check |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240402194252/https://www.chronicle.com/article/a-very-public-presidencys-reality-check |archive-date=April 2, 2024 |accessdate=2024-04-02 |newspaper=The Chronicle of Higher Education}}</ref> The strike ended on August 25, 2023, right before the start of the fall 2023 semester, when the Ono administration and GEO reached an agreement.<ref>{{cite news |date=2023-08-25 |title=University of Michigan grad student employees ratify new deal after historic strike |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/university-of-michigan-grad-student-employees-ratify-new-deal-after-historic-strike/ |accessdate=2024-04-02 |newspaper=CBS News}}</ref>

==== Israeli–Palestinian conflict ====
On October 10, 2023, Santa Ono condemned Hamas and called it "terrorists" through a campus statement.<ref>{{cite web |title=U-M statement regarding Mideast violence &#124; Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/u-m-statement-regarding-mideast-violence/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231115151824/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/u-m-statement-regarding-mideast-violence/ |archive-date=November 15, 2023 |access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref> On October 13 afternoon, around 300 University of Michigan students and community members protested outside the [[President's House, University of Michigan|President's House]], objecting to Ono's statement and criticizing Ono's views on Palestinian people, casualties, and forced displacement.<ref>{{Cite news |last2=Patil |first1=Sneha |last1=Dhandapani |first2=Sejal |date=2023-10-15 |title=Hundreds gather in Ann Arbor to protest violence in Gaza |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/campus-life/umich-safe-protests-president-onos-response-to-violence-in-middle-east/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |newspaper=[[The Michigan Daily]] |language=en-US }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Kalakailo |first=Sophia |date=2023-10-14 |title=Pro-Palestinian demonstrators protest outside University of Michigan president's house |url=https://www.mlive.com/news/ann-arbor/2023/10/pro-palestinian-demonstrators-protest-outside-university-of-michigan-presidents-house.html |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref> Ono responded with an additional statement to the university community on the same day, reaffirming his stance.<ref>{{cite web |title=Campus safety is our top priority &#124; Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/campus-safety-is-our-top-priority/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231115151824/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/campus-safety-is-our-top-priority/ |archive-date=November 15, 2023 |access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> In November, 40 pro-Palestinian students were arrested during a sit-in demonstration outside Ono's office.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Students and faculty react to UF presidential finalist |url=https://www.alligator.org/article/2025/05/students-and-faculty-react-to-uf-presidential-finalist |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=The Independent Florida Alligator |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=King |first=Jon |date=2023-11-20 |title=40 pro-Palestinian protestors arrested Friday during U of M demonstration  |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2023/11/20/40-student-protestors-arrested-friday-during-u-of-m-demonstration/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |website=Michigan Advance |language=en-US |archive-date=February 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250204082707/https://michiganadvance.com/2023/11/20/40-student-protestors-arrested-friday-during-u-of-m-demonstration/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In December, Ono canceled the central student government's campus-wide voting on two resolutions related to the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=U-M statement regarding CSG resolutions and ongoing campus tensions {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/u-m-statement-regarding-csg-resolutions-and-ongoing-campus-tensions/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=president.umich.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dhandapani |first=Sneha |date=2023-12-06 |title=UMich President Ono speaks on canceled student election |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/administration/president-ono-and-regents-release-joint-statement-on-canceled-csg-resolutions/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=STAFF |first=THE MICHIGAN DAILY NEWS |date=2023-11-30 |title=UMich cancels Israel-Palestine CSG ballot proposals before results |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/student-government/umich-cancels-voting-on-ballot-proposals-about-israel-hamas-war/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

On April 30, 2024, United States Representative [[Virginia Foxx]], in her official capacity as chair of the [[United States House Committee on Education and the Workforce]], called Santa Ono to a congressional hearing scheduled for May 23 on "antisemitic college chaos".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-30 |title=Foxx Calls on Yale, UCLA, and Michigan to Appear Before the Committee About Antisemitism |url=https://edworkforce.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=410503 |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Committee on Education & the Workforce |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |title=UM president called to testify in Washington on college's handling of antisemitism on Aug. 9 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref> On May 21, Ono cited fire safety reasons and sent police to clear the [[List of pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses in the United States in 2024#Michigan|pro-Palestinian encampment]] on [[The Diag]] in front of the [[Hatcher Graduate Library]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Powers |first=Sara |date=2024-05-21 |title=Police clear pro-Palestinian encampment at University of Michigan Diag - CBS Detroit |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/watch-police-moving-in-on-pro-palestinian-encampment-university-of-michigan/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Ending the encampment {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/messages-to-the-community/ending-the-encampment/ |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=president.umich.edu}}</ref> The encampment was first set up on April 22 to protest for [[Disinvestment from Israel|divestment]] from [[Israel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Warikoo |first1=Niraj |last2=Han |first2=Junfu |date=April 24, 2024 |title=University of Michigan students set up tent encampment, demand divestment from Israel |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2024/04/23/university-michigan-students-tent-encampment-israel-divestment/73417982007/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240424093126/https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/2024/04/23/university-michigan-students-tent-encampment-israel-divestment/73417982007/ |archive-date=April 24, 2024 |access-date=April 24, 2024 |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Four protesters were arrested.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-21 |title=VIDEOS: Police break up pro-Palestinian encampment at University of Michigan Diag; 4 arrested |url=https://www.wxyz.com/news/videos-police-raid-pro-palestinian-encampment-at-university-of-michigan-diag |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522070535/https://www.wxyz.com/news/videos-police-raid-pro-palestinian-encampment-at-university-of-michigan-diag |archive-date=May 22, 2024 |access-date=2024-05-22 |website=WXYZ 7 News Detroit |language=en}}</ref> Afterward, the United States House Committee on Education and the Workforce changed Ono's congressional testimony format to transcribed interviews instead of having him appear before the full congressional committee as initially expected.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valbrun |first=Marjorie |title=Different Hearing Format for Yale, Michigan Presidents on Campus Antisemitism |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/quick-takes/2024/05/31/new-format-yale-michigan-presidents-antisemitism-hearing |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-29 |title=Yale and Michigan Presidents Set to Participate in Transcribed Interviews |url=https://edworkforce.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=410635 |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Committee on Education & the Workforce |language=en}}</ref>

On October 10, 2024, a Michigan's local Muslim group filed a federal complaint with the [[United States Department of Education]] against the university for creating a "racially hostile environment" for Arab students. The complaint cited a leaked audio recording of president Ono discussing the "unbalanced" political pressure to crack down on antisemitism on campus, but not on Islamophobia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-10 |title=Muslim group files federal complaint against U of M, cites apparent Ono tape in filing |url=https://www.michiganpublic.org/education/2024-10-10/muslim-group-files-federal-complaint-against-u-of-m-includes-apparent-ono-tape-in-filing |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=Michigan Public |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kozlowski |first=Kim |title=Michigan Muslim group files complaint with feds after release of Ono audio |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2024/10/09/michigan-muslim-group-cair-files-complaint-with-feds-after-release-of-president-santa-ono-audio/75589647007/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Liao |first=Michelle |date=2024-10-10 |title=CAIR-MI files federal complain over leaked Ono audio recording |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/news-briefs/cair-mi-files-federal-complaint-over-leaked-ono-audio-recording/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref> On January 30, 2025, the Ono administration suspended the Students Allied for Freedom and Equality, a pro-Palestinian student group on campus, for two years, citing violations of university policy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boucher |first=Dave |title=University of Michigan suspends pro-Palestinian student group after protests |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/2025/01/31/university-michigan-suspends-pro-palestinian-students-allied-freedom-equality/78061052007/ |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Corsi |first=Marissa |date=2025-01-31 |title=UMich suspends SAFE for up to two years |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/news/news-briefs/umich-suspends-safe-for-up-to-two-years/ |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

On February 3, 2025, Ono was sued as a defendant in a federal lawsuit in the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan]] by the [[American Civil Liberties Union]] of Michigan and the Sugar Law Center for Economic and Social Justice for banning individuals who sought to engage in pro-Palestine protests from campus, including all public areas, and for threatening them with [[trespassing]] charges. The lawsuit accused Ono of unconstitutionally punishing protesters and suppressing their [[First Amendment to the United States Constitution|First Amendment]] right to [[Freedom of speech|free speech]] and their [[Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Fourteenth Amendment]] right to [[due process]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aclumich.org/app/uploads/2025/02/zou_v._ono_complaint.pdf|title=Case 2:25-cv-10315-MAG-APP|date=2025-02-03|access-date=2026-02-01|website=American Civil Liberties Union of Michigan|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201170404/www.aclumich.org/app/uploads/2025/02/zou_v._ono_complaint.pdf|archive-date=2026-02-01|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=ACLU and Sugar Law Center Sue University of Michigan to Stop Unconstitutional Banishment of Protestors from Campus|url=https://www.aclumich.org/press-releases/aclu-and-sugar-law-center-sue-university-michigan-stop-unconstitutional-banishment/|website=ACLU of Michigan|access-date=2026-02-01|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112234331/www.aclumich.org/press-releases/aclu-and-sugar-law-center-sue-university-michigan-stop-unconstitutional-banishment/|archive-date=2026-01-12|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=ACLU sues University of Michigan over campus protest policies|url=https://www.michiganpublic.org/criminal-justice-legal-system/2025-02-03/aclu-sues-university-of-michigan-over-campus-protest-policies|website=Michigan Public|date=2025-02-03|access-date=2026-02-01|language=en|first=Sarah|last=Cwiek|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311071700/www.michiganpublic.org/criminal-justice-legal-system/2025-02-03/aclu-sues-university-of-michigan-over-campus-protest-policies|archive-date=2026-03-11|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== University of Florida ===
On May 4, 2025, while serving as the 15th president of the University of Michigan, Ono became the sole finalist for the presidency post at the University of Florida.<ref name=":5" /> His May 4 resignation from all employment at the University of Michigan was accepted in writing on May 6.<ref name=":8" /> At Ono's request, the [[American Association of Colleges and Universities]] removed his previous signature on May 7 from an April 22 [[open letter]] jointly signed by more than 660 university and college leaders nationwide in opposition to "government intrusion" in higher education.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalakailo |first=Sophia |date=2025-05-08 |title=Santa Ono strikes name from letter opposing 'government intrusion' in higher ed |url=https://www.mlive.com/education/2025/05/santa-ono-strikes-name-from-letter-opposing-government-intrusion-in-higher-ed.html |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Outgoing UMich Prez Santa Ono Pulls His Name from Academic Freedom Letter |url=https://talkingpointsmemo.com/edblog/outgoing-umich-prez-santa-ono-pulls-his-name-from-academic-freedom-letter |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=TPM – Talking Points Memo |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-22 |title=A Call for Constructive Engagement |url=https://www.aacu.org/newsroom/a-call-for-constructive-engagement |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=AAC&U |language=en-US}}</ref> On May 8, Ono published an opinion article titled "Why I Chose the University of Florida" in ''Inside Higher Ed'', in which he criticized DEI policies he had previously implemented at Michigan, praised Florida's values, and described the UF presidency as "the extraordinary opportunity".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-09 |title=UMich president condemns DEI explaining why he wants to leave for U. Florida |url=https://www.thecollegefix.com/bulletin-board/umich-president-condemns-dei-explaining-why-he-wants-to-leave-for-u-florida/ |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=The College Fix}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-15 |title=A Major College-President Transition Is Defined by an About-Face on DEI |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/is-this-college-leader-anti-woke-enough-for-florida |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ono |first=Santa J. |title=Why I Chose the University of Florida |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/opinion/views/2025/05/08/why-i-chose-university-florida-santa-ono-opinion |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-03 |title=Florida Board Rejects University of Michigan President Over DEI Stance in Unprecedented Move |url=https://www.diverseeducation.com/faculty-staff/article/15747662/florida-board-rejects-university-of-michigan-president-over-dei-stance-in-unprecedented-move |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=Diverse: Issues In Higher Education |language=en-us}}</ref>

On May 27, 2025, the [[University of Florida Board of Trustees]] voted [[unanimously]] to select Ono as the incoming [[List of presidents of the University of Florida|14th president]] of the University of Florida, pending ratification from the [[Florida Board of Governors]] (the governing body of the [[State University System of Florida]]).<ref name="UF" /> Ono's draft contract with Florida included a total compensation package exceeding US$3 million per year, including a $1.5 million base salary, $500,000 for chairmanship at [[University of Florida Health|UF Health]], more than $400,000 performance bonuses, $500,000 annual raises, and extra retention incentives.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waagmeester |first=Jay |date=2025-06-02 |title=$3 million contract on the table for former U of M president who faces GOP concerns in Florida  |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2025/06/02/3-million-contract-on-the-table-for-former-u-of-m-president-who-faces-gop-concerns-in-florida/ |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=Michigan Advance |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Santa Ono contract as president of University of Florida |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/education/2025/05/29/dr-santa-ono-contract-as-president-of-university-of-florida/83918571007/ |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=Gainesville Sun}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date= May 29, 2025|title=UF Board of Trustees offers Ono base salary of $1.5 million |url=https://www.wcjb.com/2025/05/29/uf-board-trustees-offers-ono-base-salary-15-million/ |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=WCJB}}</ref>

On June 3, 2025, Ono's hire was rejected by the Florida Board of Governors in a 10–6 vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Festo |first=Alan |title=Florida Board of Governors rejects Santa Ono as University of Florida president |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/education/2025/06/03/board-of-governors-rejects-santa-ono-as-university-of-florida-president/84007003007/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US |archive-date=June 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603210325/https://www.gainesville.com/story/news/education/2025/06/03/board-of-governors-rejects-santa-ono-as-university-of-florida-president/84007003007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This decision came after a three-hour-long meeting between the board and Ono, which included discussions on Ono's support of "race-based hiring, holistic admissions, DEI and climate activism."<ref name=reject>{{Cite web |title=Board of Governors rejects Santa J. Ono as UF president |url=https://www.alligator.org/article/2025/06/board-of-governors-rejects-santa-j-ono-as-uf-president?utm_campaign=feed&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=The Independent Florida Alligator |language=en-US}}</ref> His candidacy had been questioned by national conservatives including [[Christopher Rufo]] and [[Donald Trump Jr.]], the latter of whom referred to Ono as a "woke psycho" who "might be a perfect fit for a Communist school in California".<ref name="guard-3jun2025">{{cite news |last1=Dixon |first1=Matt |title=Pick for University of Florida president rejected after a conservative backlash |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/santa-ono-rejected-university-florida-president-conservative-backlash-rcna209460 |access-date=June 3, 2025 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=June 3, 2025}}</ref> While it was reported that many of the members of the board disagreed with each other over Ono's beliefs in these and other areas, some were "praising [Ono's]...shift towards conservative values."<ref name=reject /> Media noted that progressive critics saw Ono's actions as a betrayal, conservatives questioned the sincerity of his ideological turnaround, and some viewed his conversion as opportunistic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaulis |first=Dahn |title=University of Florida Rejects Santa Ono in Favor of Right-Wing Conformity |url=https://www.highereducationinquirer.org/2025/06/university-of-florida-rejects-santa-ono.html |access-date=2025-07-25 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-03 |title=Santa Ono blocked from UF presidency amid DEI backlash |url=https://www.fox35orlando.com/news/santa-ono-blocked-from-uf-presidency-amid-dei-backlash |access-date=2025-07-25 |website=FOX 35 Orlando |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dodge |first=Samuel |date=2025-06-04 |title='Karma': Santa Ono's rejection mocked by University of Michigan community |url=https://www.mlive.com/news/ann-arbor/2025/06/karma-santa-onos-rejection-mocked-by-university-of-michigan-community.html |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=mlive |language=en}}</ref>

=== United Kingdom ===
On August 18, 2025, the Ellison Institute of Technology, Oxford Limited, a private limited company incorporated in November 2021 in [[Littlemore|Littlemore district]], [[Oxford|Oxford city]], England,<ref name=":16" /> announced the appointment of Ono as president of its global division.<ref name=":14" /> Ono would be responsible for assisting John Bell, the president of the company, in expanding its local science programs and overseeing its global affairs.<ref name=":14" /><ref name=":15">{{Cite web |date=2025-08-18 |title=Former University of Michigan president picked for education role in United Kingdom - CBS Detroit |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/santa-ono-new-role-ellison-institute/ |access-date=2025-08-19 |website=CBS News |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards ==
On April 8, 2016, on his one-day visit to [[Chiba University]] in Japan as the president of the University of Cincinnati to discuss future collaboration opportunities between the two institutions, Ono received an honorary doctorate from the Japanese university.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 19, 2016 |title=News ＆ Events｜Chiba University |url=https://www.chiba-u.ac.jp/e/others/topics/topics/2016-04-19cincinnati.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714004534/https://www.chiba-u.ac.jp/e/others/topics/topics/2016-04-19cincinnati.html |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=[[Chiba University]]}}</ref> On December 10, 2020, while serving as the UBC president, Ono received an honorary [[Doctor of Divinity|doctor of divinity]] degree from the [[Vancouver School of Theology]] of the University of British Columbia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Topping |first=Richard |date=December 10, 2020 |title=VST Announces 2021 Honorary Doctor of Divinity Recipient |url=https://vst.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/VST-Media-Release-2021-HDD-Recipient.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119120708/https://vst.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/VST-Media-Release-2021-HDD-Recipient.pdf |archive-date=January 19, 2021 |access-date=July 13, 2022 |website=[[Vancouver School of Theology]] |page=2}}</ref>

In 2017, Ono received a Professional Achievement Award from the University of Chicago Alumni Association.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://alumniandfriends.uchicago.edu/alumni-association/awardee/2017/santa-j-ono |title=2017: Professional Achievement Award Santa J. Ono, AB'84 University of Chicago Alumni Awards |publisher=University of Chicago Alumni Association |date=September 22, 2017 |accessdate=September 30, 2017 |archive-date=September 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170930222615/https://alumniandfriends.uchicago.edu/alumni-association/awardee/2017/santa-j-ono }}</ref> While serving as the UBC president, he was elected as a fellow of the [[Canadian Academy of Health Sciences]] in September 2017<ref>{{cite web |title=Two Faculty Members Become Newest Fellows of the Canadian Academy of Health Sciences |work=Faculty of Medicine, University of British Columbia |date=September 15, 2017 |url=http://www.med.ubc.ca/two-faculty-members-become-newest-fellows-of-the-canadian-academy-of-health-sciences/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018012531/http://www.med.ubc.ca/two-faculty-members-become-newest-fellows-of-the-canadian-academy-of-health-sciences/ |archive-date=October 18, 2017 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> and as a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in April 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://research.ubc.ca/aaas-elected-members-2022 |title= Dr. Catherine L. Johnson and President and Vice-Chancellor Santa J. Ono elected as members of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences |access-date= April 30, 2022 |archive-date= April 29, 2022 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220429000511/https://research.ubc.ca/aaas-elected-members-2022 |url-status= live }}</ref> While serving as the president of the University of Michigan, he was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]] of the United States in October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-21 |title=National Academy of Medicine Elects 100 New Members - NAM |url=https://nam.edu/news-and-insights/national-academy-of-medicine-elects-100-new-members-6/ |access-date=2025-08-22 |website=nam.edu |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Santa Ono was named after Santaro, a Japanese folk story character.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Danard |first=Susan |date=June 13, 2016 |title=Santa Ono comes home to UBC |url=https://news.ubc.ca/2016/06/13/santa-ono-comes-home-to-ubc/ |access-date=July 13, 2022 |website=UBC News |language=en-US |archive-date=June 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621163600/https://news.ubc.ca/2016/06/13/santa-ono-comes-home-to-ubc/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Ono, a practicing [[Anglican Communion|Anglican]], is a member of the Anglican Communion Science Commission and served as a [[Eucharistic Minister|lay Eucharistic minister.]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Todd |first=Douglas |date=June 18, 2016 |title=Santa Ono open about his Christian faith |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/staff-blogs/santa-ono-open-about-his-christian-faith |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210612231604/https://vancouversun.com/news/staff-blogs/santa-ono-open-about-his-christian-faith |archive-date=June 12, 2021 |access-date=July 13, 2022 |website=vancouversun |language=en-CA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ambrosio |first=Alicia |date=May 28, 2018 |title=Secular environment makes faith stronger: UBC president |url=https://bccatholic.ca/news/catholic-van/secular-environment-makes-faith-stronger-ubc-president |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714004558/https://bccatholic.ca/news/catholic-van/secular-environment-makes-faith-stronger-ubc-president |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |access-date=July 13, 2022 |website=The B.C. Catholic |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Anglican Communion Science Commission |url=https://www.anglicancommunion.org/community/commissions/anglican-communion-science-commission.aspx |access-date=December 5, 2023 |website=Anglican Communion}}</ref>

Ono met Gwendolyn "Wendy" Yip at McGill University in 1985; Yip was then an undergraduate student, and Ono was a graduate student.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Ryan |title=Ono, Yip recount love story, reflect on marriage |url=https://www.newsrecord.org/college_life/ono-yip-recount-love-story-reflect-on-marriage/article_bc3467d4-938c-11e3-8b3b-001a4bcf6878.html |access-date=October 12, 2022 |website=The News Record |date=February 11, 2014 |language=en |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714004517/https://www.newsrecord.org/college_life/ono-yip-recount-love-story-reflect-on-marriage/article_bc3467d4-938c-11e3-8b3b-001a4bcf6878.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The pair married in 1989 and have two daughters together.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Ryan |date=February 11, 2014 |title=Ono, Yip recount love story, reflect on marriage |url=http://www.newsrecord.org/for_the_record/love_issue/ono-yip-recount-love-story-reflect-on-marriage/article_bc3467d4-938c-11e3-8b3b-001a4bcf6878.html |work=The News Record |location=Cincinnati, Ohio |access-date=January 7, 2018 |archive-date=July 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714004423/https://www.newsrecord.org/for_the_record/love_issue/ono-yip-recount-love-story-reflect-on-marriage/article_bc3467d4-938c-11e3-8b3b-001a4bcf6878.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Wendy Yip received a Bachelor of Science with a major in immunology from McGill University in 1988 and a [[Juris Doctor]] from [[Boston University]] in 1991. Her father is Gar Lam Yip ({{Lang-zh|s=叶嘉林|labels=no}}), a [[Chinese Canadians|Chinese-Canadian]] professor of [[Electrical engineering|electrical and computer engineering]] at McGill University, and her mother is Alice Chan-Yip ({{Lang-zh|s=陈敏娜|labels=no}}), a Chinese-Canadian [[pediatrician]] based in Montreal and former board member with the [[Montreal Chinese Hospital]] ({{Lang-zh|s=满地可中华医院|labels=no}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=华人女婿小野三太成密西根大学首位亚裔校长，年薪超650万！_加拿大_美国_因为 |url=https://www.sohu.com/a/569308268_115128 |access-date=October 12, 2022 |website=www.sohu.com |archive-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015031036/https://www.sohu.com/a/569308268_115128 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gar Lam Yip Memorial Fellowship |url=https://www.mcgill.ca/engineering/yip |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=Faculty of Engineering |language=en |archive-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015031235/https://www.mcgill.ca/engineering/yip |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=General |first=Office of the Secretary to the Governor |title=Ms. Alice Mannor Chan-Yip |url=https://www.gg.ca/en/honours/recipients/146-12525 |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=The Governor General of Canada |archive-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015172104/https://www.gg.ca/en/honours/recipients/146-12525 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-12 |title=Alice Chan-Yip - McGill University |url=https://www.mcgill.ca/peds/files/peds/20181012_-_alice_chan-yip.pdf |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=McGill University |archive-date=October 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015172121/https://www.mcgill.ca/peds/files/peds/20181012_-_alice_chan-yip.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
